W2-011.decision: cut at `web:Dan.4.22`=`oshb:Dan.4.19`/`web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20` (this row ends at `web:Dan.4.22`=`oshb:Dan.4.19`; the recital verse `web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20` goes to the next row)
W2-011.claim: The close of this row cuts a sentence in two. `web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20` is a subordinate recital clause: it opens וְדִ֣י חֲזָ֣ה מַלְכָּ֡א (OSHB/WLC; Aramaic; 'and whereas the king saw') and repeats the watcher's decree, and its main clause is the next verse, דְּנָ֥ה פִשְׁרָ֖א מַלְכָּ֑א (OSHB/WLC; Aramaic) at `web:Dan.4.24`=`oshb:Dan.4.21`. Daniel's speech has two matching movements, each a recital of a dream element followed by its meaning: the tree recited at `web:Dan.4.20`-`web:Dan.4.21`=`oshb:Dan.4.17`-`oshb:Dan.4.18` and identified at `web:Dan.4.22`=`oshb:Dan.4.19`; the watcher's decree recited at `web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20` and interpreted at `web:Dan.4.24`-`web:Dan.4.26`=`oshb:Dan.4.21`-`oshb:Dan.4.23`. The row's own rationale says the turn is from the tree's identification to the decree's meaning; the decree's recital belongs to the second of those, not the first. The seam the form supports is one verse earlier.
W2-011.both_sides: The edge as drawn, `web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20`/`web:Dan.4.24`=`oshb:Dan.4.21`: the near side `web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20` closes nothing, it is a dependent clause that ends inside the quoted decree; the far side `web:Dan.4.24`=`oshb:Dan.4.21` carries the interpretation formula (this_is_the_interpretation_aram), which the book plan names as the turn. One side only. The edge proposed, `web:Dan.4.22`=`oshb:Dan.4.19`/`web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20`: the near side `web:Dan.4.22`=`oshb:Dan.4.19` completes the sentence begun at `web:Dan.4.20`=`oshb:Dan.4.17` with the identification and ends on the reach of the king's dominion; the far side `web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20` opens a new recital with the same connective that opens the third recital at `web:Dan.4.26`=`oshb:Dan.4.23`, וְדִ֣י אֲמַ֗רוּ (OSHB/WLC; Aramaic; 'and whereas they commanded'). Both sides. Against the proposal: the formula verse would then stand second in its row and not first, and no PE or SAMEKH stands at either edge, so neither is helped or hindered by the single-witness marks.

suggested_fix.fact: the verse that recites the watcher's decree is the dependent opening clause of the sentence whose main clause is the interpretation formula; the first movement of the speech ends with the identification of the tree as the king

W2-011.claim: The onset warrant is misstated on the bytes. At MT 4:16 (WEB 4:19) Daniel is not the first speaker: the verse opens with third-person narration of Daniel's dismay, then the king speaks, and only then Daniel replies. What changes at this edge is the frame: the king's first person at MT 4:15 gives way to third-person reference to the king at MT 4:16, and that third-person frame then runs to MT 4:30. The row names the weaker and inexact ground (a change of speaker from the king to Daniel) and does not state the shift of person.
W2-011.both_sides: Behind the edge: MT 4:15 is the king's own first-person charge, אֲנָ֖ה מַלְכָּ֣א נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֑ר (oshb:Dan.4.15). At the edge: MT 4:16 has עָנֵ֨ה מַלְכָּ֜א וְאָמַ֗ר (oshb:Dan.4.16), the king named in the third person and still speaking, before עָנֵ֤ה בֵלְטְשַׁאצַּר֙ וְאָמַ֔ר (oshb:Dan.4.16). So the far side supports the cut, and supports it by a shift of person that the row leaves unsaid; the cut itself stands. No PE or SAMEKH stands after MT 4:15 (MEASURED, WLC only), as the row says.

suggested_fix.fact: The onset rests on the shift from the king's first-person speech to third-person narration in which the king is named and speaks before Daniel answers; Daniel's reply is the third movement of the verse, not its opening.

W2-012.decision: cut at `web:Dan.4.22`=`oshb:Dan.4.19`/`web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20` (this row opens at `web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20`; its close stays at `web:Dan.4.27`=`oshb:Dan.4.24`)
W2-012.claim: This is the same seam as the preceding row's close, seen from the onset side, and it is one finding, not two. The row opens on the main clause of a sentence whose dependent clause, the recital of the watcher's decree at `web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20`, it leaves behind. The decree's recital and the decree's interpretation are one movement, parallel to the tree's recital and identification before it; the row should open at `web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20`. Its close at `web:Dan.4.27`=`oshb:Dan.4.24` is sound: the counsel ends Daniel's speech and the narrator's voice follows.
W2-012.both_sides: Onset as drawn: far side `web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20` is a dependent clause that does not close; near side `web:Dan.4.24`=`oshb:Dan.4.21` has the interpretation formula. One side. Onset proposed: far side `web:Dan.4.22`=`oshb:Dan.4.19` completes the identification; near side `web:Dan.4.23`=`oshb:Dan.4.20` opens the second recital with וְדִ֣י חֲזָ֣ה מַלְכָּ֡א (OSHB/WLC; Aramaic). Both sides. Close, unchanged: near side `web:Dan.4.27`=`oshb:Dan.4.24` ends the speech with the counsel; far side `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25` is the narrator, naming the king in the third person. Both sides.

suggested_fix.fact: the interpretation formula is the main clause that answers the recital of the watcher's decree in the verse before it; recital and interpretation form one movement of five verses

W2-012.claim: Two disclosure gaps, neither touching the cut. First, the English gloss in the tag at WEB 4:24 = MT 4:21 is six consecutive WEB words of that verse and stands without quotation form. Second, the WLC editorial notes at MT 4:22 (WEB 4:25), which record an anomalous form and a ketiv/qere that differs from BHS, are not disclosed although the row's span covers the verse. The Aramaic splice, the ketiv/qere list, the paseq and the zero-mark claim are all true.
W2-012.both_sides: Onset side: MT 4:20 ends the recital of the watcher's words and MT 4:21 opens with the interpretation formula; no mark follows MT 4:20, as the row says. Close side: MT 4:24 ends Daniel's speech and opens with the connective the row calls 'therefore' (first word of oshb:Dan.4.24); MT 4:25 is the narrator's notice. No mark stands between MT 4:24 and MT 4:25, so the close is unmarked; the PE comes one verse later (see W2-013).

suggested_fix.fact: The gloss either takes quotation form with its WEB reference or is recast in words that are not the translation's; and the row discloses that WLC carries editorial notes at this verse marking an anomalous form and a ketiv/qere that differs from BHS.
suggested_fix.verse: web:Dan.4.24 = oshb:Dan.4.21 for the gloss; oshb:Dan.4.22 = web:Dan.4.25 for the notes

W2-013.decision: cut at `web:Dan.4.27`=`oshb:Dan.4.24`/`web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25` and not at `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25`/`web:Dan.4.29`=`oshb:Dan.4.26` (the notice joins the fulfilment account as its opening verse; the PE after `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25` is disclosed as single-witness evidence against the join)
W2-013.claim: `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25` is not a closing notice. It is the narrator's heading for the fulfilment account, and the verse after it cannot open a unit without it: `web:Dan.4.29`=`oshb:Dan.4.26` has no expressed subject. Its Aramaic ends מְהַלֵּ֥ךְ הֲוָֽה (OSHB/WLC; Aramaic; 'he was walking') and names nobody; the king is named in `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25` and next at `web:Dan.4.30`=`oshb:Dan.4.27`. The one-verse row is parted from that account by a PE alone. The row says the PE is its chief evidence, and a mark of one witness may inform an edge but may not decide one. The unit the form gives is `web:Dan.4.28`-`web:Dan.4.33`=`oshb:Dan.4.25`-`oshb:Dan.4.30`, six verses of unbroken third-person narration.
W2-013.both_sides: Edge `web:Dan.4.27`=`oshb:Dan.4.24`/`web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25`: the near side ends Daniel's speech with the counsel; the far side changes voice to the narrator and names the king with his title. Both sides, and it stays. Edge `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25`/`web:Dan.4.29`=`oshb:Dan.4.26`: for it, a PE (WLC only) follows `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25`, and the verb of the notice, כֹּ֣לָּא מְּטָ֔א עַל (OSHB/WLC; Aramaic), takes up מְטָ֖ת עַל (OSHB/WLC; Aramaic) from the interpretation formula at `web:Dan.4.24`=`oshb:Dan.4.21`, so the notice can be read as answering the interpretation it follows. Against it, the far side `web:Dan.4.29`=`oshb:Dan.4.26` opens with a duration phrase, which is texture, and depends on `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25` for its subject; the notice says what happened before the account says how. The text-side evidence for this edge is one-sided and its only firm support is the mark. That is the edge to give up.

suggested_fix.fact: the verse after the notice names no subject and takes the king from the notice; the notice heads the fulfilment account, and the PE after it is single-witness evidence to disclose, not the ground of a one-verse unit

W2-013.claim: The Masoretic layer bounds this one-verse row on one side only, and the row weighs only the rival that the mark already excludes. In the WLC mark layer no PE or SAMEKH stands anywhere between the PE after MT 3:30 and the PE after MT 4:25: the notice at MT 4:25 (WEB 4:28) is the last verse of the open section that begins at MT 3:31 (WEB 4:1), and nothing separates it from MT 4:24 (WEB 4:27). The mark therefore favours reading the notice as the close of what precedes. The row's rejected alternative is the forward merge; the backward merge into the interpretation unit is not named.
W2-013.both_sides: Onset side (MT 4:24 / MT 4:25): no mark; the ground is a change from Daniel's speech to a narrator's sentence, כֹּ֣לָּא מְּטָ֔א עַל נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֖ר מַלְכָּֽא (oshb:Dan.4.25). The third-person frame is not new here, since it began at MT 4:16, so the onset rests on the end of the speech alone. Close side (MT 4:25 / MT 4:26): a PE, single-witness, then a time phrase and a new scene. The close is the stronger edge and the onset the weaker one; a one-verse row is defensible as a record of that tension, but its weaker edge is the one left unweighed.

suggested_fix.fact: The rival to weigh beside the forward merge is the backward one: the notice read as the close of the interpretation, since no paragraph mark divides it from the end of Daniel's speech and the open section that the petuchah closes runs up to and includes the notice.
suggested_fix.verse: oshb:Dan.4.24 / oshb:Dan.4.25 = web:Dan.4.27 / web:Dan.4.28, with the PE after oshb:Dan.4.25

W2-014.decision: cut at `web:Dan.4.27`=`oshb:Dan.4.24`/`web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25` (this row opens at `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25`; its close stays at `web:Dan.4.33`=`oshb:Dan.4.30`)
W2-014.claim: This is the same seam as the one-verse notice before it, seen from the onset side, and it is one finding, not two. The row's first verse, `web:Dan.4.29`=`oshb:Dan.4.26`, has no expressed subject and a duration phrase for an opener; the row itself says its onset rests on the PE and on the change from summary to scene. The king whom the verse describes is named in the notice at `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25`, which belongs at the head of this account. The close at `web:Dan.4.33`=`oshb:Dan.4.30` is sound: the fulfilment notice ends the judgment, and the next verse returns to the king's own voice.
W2-014.both_sides: Onset as drawn: far side `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25` is followed by a PE (WLC only) and echoes the verb of the interpretation formula; near side `web:Dan.4.29`=`oshb:Dan.4.26` is a subjectless clause opened by a duration phrase (texture). The text gives the near side nothing that opens. Onset proposed: far side `web:Dan.4.27`=`oshb:Dan.4.24` ends Daniel's speech; near side `web:Dan.4.28`=`oshb:Dan.4.25` is the narrator naming the king. Both sides. Close, unchanged: near side `web:Dan.4.33`=`oshb:Dan.4.30` reports the fulfilment (at_that_moment_aram); far side `web:Dan.4.34`=`oshb:Dan.4.31` has i_nebuchadnezzar_aram, lifted_eyes_aram and blessed_aram and a second time phrase. Both sides.

suggested_fix.fact: the opening verse of the scene names no subject; the king is named in the notice before it, which heads the account of the fulfilment

W2-014.claim: The onset is the one edge in this cluster's interior that the Masoretic layer marks: a PE follows MT 4:25, and MT 4:26 (WEB 4:29) opens with the time phrase the tag quotes exactly. The fulfilment formula stands at MT 4:30, one ketiv/qere note stands at MT 4:29 and none elsewhere in MT 4:26-30, and no paseq stands in the span; the row claims none.
W2-014.both_sides: Onset side: PE after MT 4:25 (single-witness) and a change from summary notice to scene. Close side: MT 4:30 reports the execution in the third person; MT 4:31 returns to the king's first person with a time phrase. No mark follows MT 4:30, so the close rests on the return of the first person, which the bytes bear out (the self-naming form stands at MT 4:31).

W3-005.claim: 5:17-5:24 holds one movement (refusal, recital of the father's humbling, charge against the son, the hand sent) and medium_low is the honest grade for its close inside one speech; but device_notes sets EXTRACTED beside a reading (that the formulas recall the father's humbling), and strongest_rejected_alternative carries a count and a weighing with no tier word.
W3-005.both_sides: Onset 5:16/5:17: two-sided, see W3-004. Close 5:24/5:25: close side, 5:24 opens with then_aram (weak alone) and its 'from before him' depends on the God named at the end of 5:23, so it leans back on the charge; onset side, 5:25 presents the writing and 5:26 carries the interpretation formula. But 5:24 ends on the writing being inscribed and 5:25 takes up those very words (read in Dan_oshb.txt Dan.5.24 and Dan.5.25), so the two verses are also chained forward. Same speaker, no mark. 5:24 is a hinge verse; an edge at 5:23/5:24 is a second live rival beside the whole-speech one.

suggested_fix.fact: the inventory holds the presence of most_high_aram at 5:18 and 5:21 and of the recognition refrain at 5:21 (EXTRACTED); that they recall the father's humbling, and that the praise of 5:23 inverts 5:4, are readings (INFERRED); the rejected rival's 12 verses is a count and its 'distinct speech functions' a weighing, each owing a tier; 5:24 is a hinge whose last clause is taken up by 5:25

W3-005.claim: The close at 5:24/5:25 is argued without two facts of the Aramaic that bear on it. First, oshb:Dan.5.24 opens on the then-connective, which the device inventory lists at this verse and the row does not name; with it the speech leaves the second-person charge of 5:22-5:23 for a third-person report of the hand and the writing. Second, the last three words of oshb:Dan.5.24 are taken up, reordered, by the first four words of oshb:Dan.5.25, which opens with the conjunction; the row's cut falls between the two halves of that repetition. The row's mark, count and quotation facts are otherwise true, and no mark follows 5:23 or 5:24.
W3-005.both_sides: Near side (5:24): opens on the then-connective, shifts from address to report, and ends on the words for this writing inscribed. Far side (5:25): opens with the conjunction and the same three lexemes, then gives the inscription; 5:26 opens the listed interpretation formula. So 5:24 looks both ways: it closes the indictment by naming its consequence and it introduces the writing that 5:25 reads. A cut after 5:23 would put the connective at a unit head and keep the repetition whole; the cut after 5:24 keeps cause and consequence together. No mark decides it. This weighing is INFERRED; the row's medium-low grade and its live rival are right, and I propose no move of the cut, only that the rationale weigh the seam with these facts and name the cut after 5:23 as a rival.

suggested_fix.fact: the then-connective stands at the head of this verse and is listed in the device inventory (EXTRACTED); the verse's closing words on the inscribed writing are repeated at the head of the next verse, which opens with the conjunction (EXTRACTED from the WLC text); a cut one verse earlier is a rival to be weighed (INFERRED)

W3-006.claim: 5:25-5:28 is a coherent unit of the right type (the writing presented, then glossed word by word under the interpretation formula at 5:26), but its grade is rounded up: its onset edge at 5:24/5:25 is the same edge the neighbouring row grades medium_low, it has no mark, no change of speaker, and 5:25 takes up the closing words of 5:24.
W3-006.both_sides: Onset 5:24/5:25: close side, 5:24 ends the charge by naming the hand and the writing; onset side, 5:25 opens with a conjunction and repeats the words for the writing being inscribed from the end of 5:24, then lists the words; the interpretation formula comes only at 5:26. One speaker throughout, no mark. The evidence for an onset at 5:25 is a change of speech function alone, and the catchword pulls the other way. Close 5:28/5:29: close side, the third gloss ends the speech; onset side, 5:29 opens with then_aram and narrated action by the king. That edge is two-sided, without a mark.

suggested_fix.fact: the onset at 5:25 rests on a shift of speech function only, inside one speech, with no mark, and 5:25 repeats the closing words of 5:24; a seam with evidence of that kind is graded medium_low, the grade the adjoining row already gives the same edge

W3-006.claim: The row's facts for 5:25-5:28 hold: the mark layer has no paragraph mark, paseq, ketiv/qere site or editorial note in these four verses and the row claims none; the interpretation formula is listed at 5:26; the then-connective is listed at 5:29; both quotations are exact and verse-initial at oshb:Dan.5.25 and oshb:Dan.5.26; the speaker does not change across the onset.
W3-006.both_sides: Onset: 5:24, on the far side, already names the writing and opens on the then-connective; 5:25 repeats its closing words and opens with the conjunction, so the onset is the weaker of the row's two seams and rests, as the row says, on the turn from report to the inscription and its glosses. Close: 5:28 gives the third of three glosses; 5:29 opens on the then-connective with the king acting. The close is firm; the row's medium grade is fair for the pair. The onset's linkage is carried as the finding on the neighbouring row.

W3-010.claim: The device inventory labels its blessed_aram hit at oshb:Dan.6.11 (web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11) as the homograph for kneeling, not blessing. The row lists blessed_aram as a signal 'in the prayer verse' and as a tag without that label, so it presents a blessing formula the verse does not hold.
W3-010.both_sides: The boundaries stand. Onset: web:Dan.6.9 = oshb:Dan.6.10 ends the conspiracy with the signing; web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11 opens with Daniel as fronted subject and a when-clause, and it does not open with the weak connective. Against the onset: web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11 ends on a habitual clause (he did as before), a SAMEKH follows it, and web:Dan.6.11 = oshb:Dan.6.12 opens with the weak connective plus the assembling verb, so the prayer verse can also be read as the close of the interdict unit. Close: web:Dan.6.15 = oshb:Dan.6.16 is the officials' last speech, again opened by the assembling verb; web:Dan.6.16 = oshb:Dan.6.17 is the king's command and the casting. Medium-low is right for both edges.

suggested_fix.fact: The inventory's hit in this verse is the verb for kneeling (he knelt on his knees); the verse holds prayer and thanksgiving but no blessing formula, and the tag is kept only with that label.

W3-010.claim: The row presents a 'blessed' formula in the prayer verse web:Dan.6.10 = oshb:Dan.6.11 (tag list, substrate signal, and device_notes with the tier EXTRACTED from the device inventory). On the bytes the matched word is the participle of kneeling, in the phrase 'kneeling on his knees'; the device inventory itself labels this hit as 'he knelt', not 'bless'. The layer does not hold a blessing here, and the row does not disclose the homograph.
W3-010.both_sides: The finding does not move a seam. Onset: no mark after MT 6:10; MT 6:11 opens with a temporal clause and no then-connective (true on the bytes, as the row says). Close: MT 6:16 and MT 6:17 both open with the then-connective and no mark stands between them; the close rests on content, as graded. The setumah after MT 6:11 is interior and disclosed. No cut proposed.

suggested_fix.fact: the inventory hit at this verse is a homograph: the word means kneeling (WEB 'he kneeled on his knees'), not blessing, and the inventory says so; the row should either drop the tag and signal or state the homograph beside them

W3-014.claim: The grade high is argued from the close alone. The row's onset edge, between the end of the doxology in web:Dan.6.27 = oshb:Dan.6.28 and the notice in web:Dan.6.28 = oshb:Dan.6.29, is the same edge the preceding row grades medium from its side; it has no mark and no formula on the notice side. A one-verse row cannot stand higher than its weaker edge, and this is the only high in the book's 75 rows.
W3-014.both_sides: Onset edge: close side, the letter's doxology ends in web:Dan.6.27 = oshb:Dan.6.28; onset side, web:Dan.6.28 = oshb:Dan.6.29 opens with a conjoined subject-first clause on Daniel in the narrator's voice; no mark after oshb:Dan.6.28. That is a real edge resting on voice and clause form, of medium strength. Close edge: web:Dan.6.28 = oshb:Dan.6.29 is a regnal summary naming two reigns; a PE follows oshb:Dan.6.29 (WLC only); 7:1 opens with a dateline that restarts the regnal sequence. That edge is as strong as any in the book. The unit and both boundaries stand; only the grade moves.

suggested_fix.fact: The grade answers to both edges of the notice: the close is strong (regnal summary, then a dateline), and the onset rests on the change from the king's voice to the narrator's with no mark, the same edge the letter's row grades medium.

W3-014.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative gives a count ('two reigns') with no tier, and device_notes names the ketiv/qere layer with no tier word. The facts hold: the verse names the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus, the petuchah follows MT 6:29, the ketiv/qere of the verse is on its last word and outside the splice, and MT 7:1 is a regnal dateline in the inventory. The close and its high confidence are supported.
W3-014.both_sides: Onset: no mark between MT 6:28 and MT 6:29; the near side turns from participles about God to a third-person statement about Daniel. Close: PE after MT 6:29 on the near side (single witness, the heavier of the two marks) and a regnal dateline opening MT 7:1 on the far side. Two independent kinds of evidence, one on each side. Confidence stands. No cut proposed.

suggested_fix.fact: the verse names two reigns, a count that can be read off the verse; give it its tier, and give the ketiv/qere disclosure the tier of the layer it names

W4-008.claim: The boundaries 7:28/8:1 and 8:4/8:5 hold as form, and medium_low is the honest grade for a behold step inside one vision. The defect is in the rejected-alternative field: it says the 8:4/8:5 edge is the only internal cut of the twelve-verse report with a device on its onset side. The device inventory holds devices on the onset side of three other candidate edges: 8:3 carries the lifted-eyes formula, the behold formula and the seeing verb; 8:4 opens on the seeing verb; 8:6 carries the seeing verb. The row's own rationale names the 8:3 devices as interior. So the stated ground is contradicted by the layer, it carries no tier, and the rival it hides (setting 8:1-8:2 against the ram from 8:3) is never weighed.
W4-008.both_sides: No cut is proposed. For the unweighed rival edge 8:2/8:3: close side, 8:2 ends the setting (Susa, the river) and repeats the seeing-in-the-vision clause; onset side, 8:3 has the lifted-eyes formula, which the inventory finds in two verses of the book (8:3 and 10:5), with the behold formula and the first animal. For the edge taken, 8:4/8:5: close side, 8:4 ends on the ram doing his will and growing great; onset side, 8:5 has the seer's own clause and the behold formula. Both edges have devices on the onset side; the row keeps the setting with the ram, which is defensible, but it must say so on true grounds.

suggested_fix.fact: Devices stand on the onset side of 8:3 (lifted-eyes formula, behold formula, seeing verb), 8:4 (seeing verb, first word) and 8:6 (seeing verb) as well as 8:5; the 8:4/8:5 edge is preferred because it is where the vision passes from the first animal to the second, not because it alone has a device. The 8:2/8:3 rival (setting against vision) is to be named and weighed, with its tier.

W4-008.claim: The rejected-alternative field says the seam 8:4/8:5 is the only internal seam of 8:1-8:12 with a device on its onset side. The bytes do not hold that: 8:3 opens on the lifted-eyes formula and the behold particle, which the row itself splices, and 8:7 opens on a first-person seeing verb. The cut at 8:4/8:5 itself is sound on the Hebrew and stays.
W4-008.both_sides: Onset 7:28/8:1: behind, the Aramaic closing notice and PE after Dan.7.28 (single witness); inside, the Hebrew regnal dateline at Dan.8.1 and the return to Hebrew at word 1 of the verse (language-zone layer run H from Dan.8.1 w1). Both sides agree; high is right. Close 8:4/8:5: inside, Dan.8.4 ends on the ram doing his will and growing great; across, Dan.8.5 opens on a first-person periphrastic clause and the behold particle. No paragraph mark stands at 8:4/8:5 in the single witness, which is not counter-evidence. A scene step inside one vision; medium_low stands.

suggested_fix.fact: Within 8:1-8:12 three verses open on a seeing or behold device: 8:3 (lifted eyes, saw, behold), 8:5 (behold after the seer's own clause) and 8:7 (first-person seeing verb with object suffix). The 8:4/8:5 seam is preferred because it divides the ram from the goat and leaves two rows of legal length, not because it is the only seam with a device. State it as a weighing, with its tier.

W4-011.claim: The span 8:15-8:18 is rightly bounded, but its unit_type is not the type the verses have. The four verses narrate, in the first person, the seer's search, a figure appearing, a voice commissioning Gabriel, the approach, the seer's fear and fall, a deep sleep and being set upright; the only interpretive words are the second half of 8:17. The closed vocabulary defines narrative to include first-person framing in the visions and defines interpretation as the reading of a vision. The row's own device note says the span is largely narrative and discloses the type as a deviation. The reading itself begins at 8:19, which the next row holds.
W4-011.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Onset 8:14/8:15: 8:14 ends the audition; 8:15 has vayehi_heb, i_daniel_heb and behold_heb. Close 8:18/8:19: 8:18 ends the collapse with the seer set upright; 8:19 has only the weak speech verb and the announcement, and it resumes the speech begun in 8:17 (both verses end on the end-time phrase), so medium_low is honest. The turn from report to interpretation that the strategy places at 8:15 is the turn of the chapter, not the type of these four verses.

suggested_fix.fact: 8:15-8:18 is first-person narrative framing (appearance, commission, collapse, restoration) that introduces the interpretation; the type that the closed vocabulary gives such framing is narrative, and the single interpretive clause at the end of 8:17 can be disclosed in the device note.

W4-011.claim: device_notes says the Aramaic figure of 7:13 is 'spliced above' and tiers the comparison EXTRACTED; no field of the row holds any byte of Dan.7.13. The comparison itself is true in the witness. Three glosses in boundary_rationale do not match their splices in extent (8:16, 8:18, 8:19). Every tier word otherwise tests true against its named layer and both edges stand.
W4-011.both_sides: Onset 8:14/8:15: behind, Dan.8.14 ends the answer; inside, Dan.8.15 opens with the narrative past, the seer's name, his search and the behold particle. No mark in the single witness; medium stands. Close 8:18/8:19: inside, Dan.8.18 ends with the seer touched and stood on his place; across, Dan.8.19 opens with a bare speech verb and a first-person announcement particle. The speaker does not change across the seam (he already speaks at 8:17), so the far side offers only the announcement; medium_low is the right grade and the row says so.

suggested_fix.fact: The address of 8:17 is Hebrew and the figure of 7:13 is Aramaic and differently worded; if the row says the Aramaic is shown it must carry the exact two words from Dan.7.13 with their reference, and otherwise it should say only that the 8:17 address is the one shown. Each gloss should cover exactly the words spliced: at 8:16 the splice stops before the object noun that the gloss translates.

W5-002.claim: The cut at 9:14/9:15 is defensible and the grade medium_low is honest, but the sentence that justifies the 11-verse span says 9:4-9:14 has no internal formula, mark or dateline under an EXTRACTED tag. The device inventory holds a formula inside the span at 9:7 (the ascription of righteousness to the Lord), which the row itself lists among its signals and quotes; and the statement that the span is one uninterrupted speech act, the confession, under the same tag is a reading, since the quoted speech that opens at 9:4 runs unbroken to 9:19.
W5-002.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Onset 9:3/9:4: narrated preparation behind, speech introduction and address formula in front. Close 9:14/9:15: 9:14 ends the retrospect on the refrain of not obeying; 9:15 opens with וְעַתָּ֣ה (oshb:Dan.9.15, OSHB/WLC), the adverb that conventionally turns a Hebrew prayer from review to request, and the same word recurs at 9:17. Against the edge, 9:15 still recalls the exodus and still confesses, and the first request stands at 9:16. Evidence stands on both sides but is soft on the far side, so medium_low is right.

suggested_fix.fact: Inside 9:4-9:14 the inventory records one formula, the ascription of righteousness at 9:7, and it does not open a unit; no mark and no dateline stand in the span. That the span is the confession part of a prayer running 9:4-9:19 is a reading (INFERRED), not a witness fact.
suggested_fix.verse: Dan 9:7 (formula) and Dan 9:4-9:19 (extent of the speech)

W5-002.claim: boundary_rationale ends by saying the 11-verse span has no internal formula, mark or dateline, tiered EXTRACTED OSHB/WLC. The mark and dateline parts hold. The formula part does not hold as written: the device inventory's formula family has hits inside the span at 9:7 (the righteousness ascription) and at 9:8, 9:10, 9:13 and 9:14 (the divine name), and the row lists those same hits among its own signals. W5-002.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Onset 9:3/9:4: no mark; 9:3 is narration, 9:4 opens with the verb of praying and the address stands at words 8-10. Close 9:14/9:15: no mark; 9:14 ends on the splice the row cites (its last three words), and 9:15 opens on the transition particle with a vocative (words 1-3) yet closes on two first-person confession verbs (its last two words חָטָ֖אנוּ רָשָֽׁעְנוּ), so the far side still confesses and the row's soft grading and medium_low confidence fit the bytes.

suggested_fix.fact: Inside 9:4-9:14 the inventory holds formula hits (the righteousness ascription at 9:7; the divine name at 9:8, 9:10, 9:13 and 9:14); none is an onset formula, and no paragraph mark and no dateline stand inside the span.

W6-004.claim: device_notes states, under the tier EXTRACTED, that the translation at 10:19 gives the greeting and stops, and that the Hebrew clause in which Daniel is strengthened and asks his lord to speak has no English counterpart. That is false. The WEB witness carries the second half of 10:19 on a continuation line after a paragraph break inside the verse. W6-004.both_sides: Onset 10:14/10:15: the first speech is over; 10:15 resumes and the seer goes mute. Close 10:19/10:20: 10:19 ends with the seer's request that his lord speak; 10:20 answers with a question that frames the long speech. The close joins a request to its answer, so it is two-sided but soft, and medium_low stands. No cut is proposed.

W6-004.claim: The row states under an EXTRACTED tier that the WEB text at 10:19 stops after the greeting and has no English counterpart for the Hebrew closing clause. That is false on the WEB bytes: verse 10:19 has a second line that renders the clause, the counterpart of the Hebrew the row quotes.
W6-004.both_sides: No cut proposed; the edge at 10:19/10:20 does not move. Near side: 10:19 ends with the seer's consent in both witnesses. Far side: 10:20 opens with a speech formula and the messenger's question. The row's own weighing (held low, same speaker) stands.

W6-008.claim: The rejected alternative is not stated at its strongest. The row declines an edge at 11:19/11:20 because it would leave 11:20 as a one-verse unit. It would not have to: 11:20 can open the following unit, which then runs 11:20-11:28, nine verses, inside the size the book's plan allows. On that reading the fall at 11:19 closes a career and the succession formula at 11:20 does what it does elsewhere, open. The row as cut ends on a verse that begins with an onset formula, and its close-side warrant cites that formula as close evidence. I do not find the form evidence strong enough to move the cut, so the cut and the medium_low grade stand; the field should name the real rival.
W6-008.both_sides: Edge as cut, 11:20/11:21: close side, the short reign is ended inside 11:20 (web:Dan.11.20 “within few days he shall be destroyed”); onset side, the succession formula at 11:21. Rival edge, 11:19/11:20: close side, 11:19 ends a career (web:Dan.11.19 “he will stumble and fall”); onset side, the same formula at 11:20. Each edge has a close and the same onset formula. What separates them is where the one verse 11:20 goes, and either way it sits in a unit of seven to nine verses.

suggested_fix.fact: an edge at 11:19/11:20 need not isolate 11:20: joined forward, 11:20 opens a nine-verse unit ending at 11:28, with the fall of 11:19 as the close before it and the second formula at 11:21 inside it; that is the rival to weigh, and the close-side fact in 11:20 is the reign's end, not the formula

W6-008.claim: The row calls 11:17, 11:18 and 11:19 the set-face formula. On the bytes only 11:17 has the verb of setting (וְיָשֵׂ֣ם פָּ֠נָיו); 11:18 is the verse's K/Q site and it stands on that very verb (the witness prints the unpointed written form, וישב פָּנָ֛יו, and only the read form is the verb of setting); 11:19 has the verb of turning (וְיָשֵׁ֣ב פָּנָ֔יו). The row discloses the 11:18 K/Q as a reading-form matter without saying that its claimed formula there rests on the read form.
W6-008.both_sides: No cut proposed; the formula is texture and opens no unit, as the row says. Onset 11:13/11:14: return in force behind, the in-those-times phrase ahead. Close 11:20/11:21: the succession wording stands on both sides (opening 11:20 and 11:21), which the row states, taking the second and tiering the choice INFERRED.

suggested_fix.fact: the face idiom has the verb of setting at 11:17 and the verb of turning at 11:19; at 11:18 the written form agrees with 11:19 and the read form with 11:17, so the K/Q at 11:18 is on the verb of the idiom

W6-010.claim: The row says 11:35 ends with the time-of-the-end phrase. It does not: the phrase stands at words 8-10 of 13, and the verse ends with a further clause on the appointed time (words 11-13). That last word is the word that opens the row at 11:29 word 1, and the same clause ends 11:27. The correction strengthens the unit (the appointed-time word frames 11:29-11:35) and it bears on the neighbouring edge at 11:28/11:29, since the same clause closes 11:27.
W6-010.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Onset 11:28/11:29: 11:28 closes a campaign with a doubled return; 11:29 opens with the appointed-time word, a temporal phrase and not a formula. Close 11:35/11:36: 11:35 carries the time-of-the-end phrase mid-verse and ends on the appointed-time clause; 11:36 opens by naming the king as subject with the do-as-he-pleases phrase, which also stands at 11:3 and 11:16. The close is the better marked of the two edges; the low grade rests on the onset.

suggested_fix.fact: In 11:35 the time-of-the-end phrase is followed by a closing clause on the appointed time, so the verse ends on the appointed-time word, the word that opens 11:29 and that also ends 11:27.

W6-010.claim: The row says oshb:Dan.11.35 ENDS with the time-of-the-end phrase. It does not. The quoted three words are an exact substring of 11:35 but stand mid-verse (words 8-10 of 13, at the main pause); the verse ends three words later with a different clause, on the appointed-time word. The WEB quotation beside it is likewise not verse-final in web:Dan.11.35.
W6-010.both_sides: No cut is proposed and the edge 11:35/11:36 stands. Close side: 11:35 holds the time-of-the-end phrase before its last clause and ends on the appointed-time word, the same word that opens 11:29, so the row's first and last words in the Masoretic text are the same lexeme; a like clause ends 11:27. Far side: 11:36 opens with the king doing as he wills (byte-collated at offset 0), a new characterization. Onset side 11:28/11:29 is one-sided, as the row says.

W6-013.claim: The row's rejected-alternative field says the SAMEKH after 12:2 and the PE after 12:3 are counted as two witnesses. They are two marks in one witness (the mark layer is WLC only), as the row's own rationale says. The same field also says an edge after 12:2 would part 12:3 from the wise of 12:3's own promise, which names the same verse on both sides; what such an edge parts is the awakening of 12:2 from the shining of the wise in 12:3. The span and both edges stand.
W6-013.both_sides: No cut is proposed. Onset 11:45/12:1: close side, the end-notice of 11:45; onset side, the at-that-time phrase, twice in 12:1 (words 1 and 22). Close 12:4/12:5: close side, the address to the seer by name with the sealing charge, which ends the speech (12:13 closes the book with the same fronted address word); onset side, 12:5 resumes first-person report with the seeing verb, the seer's name and the behold word. The two interior marks (SAMEKH after 12:2, PE after 12:3) fall inside the speech and neither coincides with a turn of speaker or scene.

W6-013.claim: The rejected-alternative field ends by saying the two marks are counted as two witnesses. The mark layer is one witness (WLC/OSHB); a SAMEKH after 12:2 and a PE after 12:3 are two marks of two different kinds from that one witness. The same row's rationale correctly calls both single-witness, so the row contradicts itself on the count of witnesses, and the count carries no tier.
W6-013.both_sides: No cut is proposed; confidence medium_low stands. The Masoretic layer does NOT support this edge: it has a PE after 12:3 and nothing after 12:4. So the mark stands on the rival's side, and the stronger of the two kinds at that. The row discloses this and decides on speaker and scene; on the other hand 12:4's sealing words recur at 12:9 and its opening pronoun recurs at 12:13, which is lexical support for the rival that the row does not mention. Onset 11:45/12:1: closing notice behind, at-that-time phrase ahead; no mark.

suggested_fix.fact: After 12:2 the single witness has a SAMEKH and after 12:3 a PE: two marks, unequal in kind, one witness; neither is merged with the other.

W6-014.claim: The edge at 12:8/12:9 parts a question from its answer. 12:8 does not end on the seer's failure to understand; its second half is his question to the man (words 5-9), and 12:9 is the reply. The row declines a cut at 12:6/12:7 because it would split a question from the oath that answers it, then accepts the same kind of split at 12:8/12:9. What supports the edge is the PE after 12:8 (one witness) and a change of speaker introduced by a plain and-he-said, which is a weak connective. The rival that keeps the pairs whole, 12:5-12:13 as one unit of nine verses, is within the size target and was declined on that mark; a second rival, an edge at 12:7/12:8, was not weighed at all.
W6-014.both_sides: No cut is proposed by this lane; the seam goes to the end review as mark-led. At 12:8/12:9: close side, 12:8 words 1-4 answer the oath just heard (the hearing verb of 12:7 word 1 returns at 12:8 word 2), but words 5-9 open a new exchange with a question; onset side, 12:9 opens with and-he-said and the reply, with no formula of its own; a PE follows 12:8. At the unweighed rival 12:7/12:8: close side, the oath ends on the finishing of all these things; onset side, 12:8 opens with the fronted first-person pronoun, and its question ends on the same demonstrative; against it, the hearing verb binds 12:8 back to 12:7 and the PE stands one verse later. 12:8 faces both ways, so neither edge is clean.

suggested_fix.fact: 12:8 ends with the seer's question and 12:9 answers it, so an edge at 12:8/12:9 divides a question from its answer and rests on the PE after 12:8 (one witness) with a weak connective; the rivals to weigh are 12:5-12:13 as one unit of nine verses and an edge at 12:7/12:8, where 12:8 opens with the fronted first-person pronoun.
